_meta.description: Policy & catalyst layer — regime cards, fiscal programs mapped to tickers, levers-to-watch. Updated: 2026-08-03.

fields.programs: Fiscal programs + direct spending mapped to tickers
fields.levers: Upcoming policy decisions that could move markets

regimes.title: China REE Export Controls
regimes.summary: China placed seven heavy/medium REEs under export licensing in April 2025 (Sm, Gd, Tb, Dy, Lu, Sc, Y — plus alloys, oxides, magnets). A second tranche of 5 additional elements was deferred to November 10, 2026. The April controls were never suspended — the 'pause' narrative was a misread. An extraterritorial '50% rule' applies: products made outside China using Chinese-origin REEs also require export licenses.
regimes.impact: Bullish for Western REE producers; creates urgency for allied-nation supply chains; adds a floor under NdPr prices.
regimes.watch: November 10, 2026 — second tranche cliff. Any guidance update from MOFCOM on application processing backlogs.

regimes.title: China Antimony Export Ban
regimes.summary: China banned antimony exports (effective October 2024) covering antimony ore, concentrates, and processed products. China produces ~50% of global antimony. Antimony trioxide is essential for flame retardants, lead-acid batteries, and military pyrotechnics. PPTA's Stibnite mine in Idaho is the only significant undeveloped Western antimony source.
regimes.impact: Direct catalyst for Perpetua Resources; creates urgency for DoD and allies to secure Stibnite permitting.
regimes.watch: Stibnite EIS completion and permitting decision. DoD funding tranche triggers.

regimes.title: Russian Uranium Import Ban (US)
regimes.summary: Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act signed May 2024. Russia (TENEX) supplied ~28% of US SWU — now banned with limited waivers expiring 2028. Forces Western enrichment rebuild. Centrus is the only US company with active enrichment capacity. Kazatomprom (Kazakhstan) is the swing uranium miner — geopolitically ambiguous (Russian/Chinese sphere influence).
regimes.impact: Structural demand floor under LEU; long-term bullish for all Western uranium supply chain.
regimes.watch: Waiver expiration schedule (2028). HALEU commercial scale timeline. Western enrichment investment commitments.

regimes.title: IRA Critical Minerals & 45X Credits
regimes.summary: Inflation Reduction Act Section 45X provides production tax credits for US-manufactured clean energy components including battery cells, modules, and critical mineral processing. FEOC (Foreign Entity of Concern) rules exclude Chinese-origin materials from EV credit eligibility — creating direct demand for US/allied REE and lithium supply. Credits scale down after 2029.
regimes.impact: Accelerates US/allied critical mineral processing investment; creates above-market margins for qualifying US producers.
regimes.watch: Congressional risk: any repeal of 45X or FEOC rules would remove the IRA reshoring premium. FEOC guidance updates from Treasury.

regimes.title: Section 232 — Copper & Derivatives
regimes.summary: Section 232 investigation into copper imports initiated February 2025. If tariffs imposed, US copper prices would decouple (upward) from LME. FCX and SCCO are the largest US copper producers — tariffs would benefit them via domestic price premium. Decision timeline: typically 270 days from initiation.
regimes.impact: Potentially very bullish for US copper producers; creates domestic price floor above LME.
regimes.watch: Commerce Department determination. Tariff rate and product scope if imposed. LME/US spread if tariffs pass.

regimes.title: CHIPS Act — Semiconductor Fab Buildout
regimes.summary: CHIPS and Science Act ($52.7B) funding new semiconductor fabs in the US. Intel Fab 52/62 (Arizona), TSMC Phoenix, Samsung Austin, Micron Idaho in various stages of build. Each fab is a major consumer of industrial gases (LIN, APD on-site), specialty materials (LIN, Resonac), copper (interconnects), and water (ERII RO systems).
regimes.impact: Creates long-term recurring revenue for on-site industrial gas contracts (15-20 year sole-source). Accelerates US specialty materials demand.
regimes.watch: Fab construction progress and production ramp timelines. Intel restructuring impact on Fab 52/62 plans.

regimes.title: Resource Nationalism — LatAm Lithium & Copper
regimes.summary: Chile (lithium nationalization announced 2023, SQM concession renegotiated through 2060), Mexico (nationalized lithium resources 2022), Bolivia (state lithium company dominant). Copper: Peru has seen repeated mine blockades (Las Bambas, Antapaccay). Argentina's provinces are more mining-friendly. The trend is toward larger government royalty/equity stakes in mineral projects.
regimes.impact: Increases country risk premium for LatAm exposure. Justifies streaming structures (FNV, WPM) — streams are above the mine-level political risk.
regimes.watch: Chile government position on further nationalization. Peru mining conflict recurrence. Argentina Milei government mining reform progress.

regimes.title: Production-Origin Bans via Equipment Authorisation
regimes.summary: A THIRD kind of control, distinct from the two this map already tracks. Export controls govern what may be sold abroad; entity lists govern who is barred. This governs WHERE A THING IS BUILT, and enforces it through the radio certification gate rather than trade law — which is why it reaches consumer and commercial hardware that Commerce controls never touched. Written to generalise: the same instrument has already been used for uncrewed aircraft systems and consumer-grade routers, and further product classes are reportedly being drafted. FIRST INSTANCE RELEVANT HERE — FCC Public Notice DA 26-786 (PSHSB), released 2026-07-28, added foreign-produced connected power inverters to the Covered List. ADOPTED AND IN FORCE, not a proposal. COVERED: a device that converts DC to AC or AC to DC AND contains components enabling remote communication, control, sensing, data collection or monitoring via Wi-Fi, cellular, Bluetooth or similar connections — the definition enumerates microinverters, string inverters, central inverters and hybrid battery-based inverters. No kW threshold was found in any source, so it runs from a rooftop microinverter to utility scale. 'FOREIGN-PRODUCED' MEANS PLACE OF PRODUCTION, NOT NATIONALITY. The test is failure to qualify as a 'domestic end product' under the Buy American standard at 48 CFR 25.101(a), which for most manufactured goods requires US manufacture AND domestic components exceeding 65% of total component cost for items delivered CY2024-2028. A German, Japanese or Korean producer is caught on identical terms to a Chinese one, and a US-headquartered brand building in Mexico or Vietnam is caught. Note the consequence of the CONTENT test: US final assembly alone does not clear it. MECHANISM: covered equipment cannot receive FCC equipment authorisation (47 CFR 2.903(a)), and applicants must certify their equipment is not covered (47 CFR 2.911(d)(5)(i)) — which bars import, marketing and sale. PROSPECTIVE ONLY: previously authorised models, already-acquired devices, and federal government purchases and use are unaffected. The damage curve is therefore a slow product-cycle strangle, not a cliff. EXIT: case-by-case Conditional Approval from the Department of War or DHS.
regimes.impact: A policy-manufactured onshoring mandate on the grid-hardware and storage stack. It is NOT a China ban — it is an everywhere-but-here ban with a discretionary licence, so the beneficiary set is 'whoever can certify US production at >65% domestic content', which is a materially smaller group than 'whoever is not Chinese'. Upstream, a binding US-production requirement pulls demand into US assembly and therefore onto power semiconductors (SiC and IGBT modules), magnetics, copper windings, capacitors, aluminium enclosures and enclosure steel. WHERE THE BOTTLENECK ACTUALLY SITS — tested rather than assumed: inverter final assembly is comparatively easy to stand up and both Enphase and SolarEdge already run US lines, so assembly is not the binding constraint. The constraint is (a) the 65% DOMESTIC CONTENT test, which reaches back into a component tier — power semis, magnetics, passives — that is largely not domestic, and (b) the Conditional Approval queue, which has no published review timetable. Both are consistent with the prior; assembly capacity is not.
regimes.watch: Whether any Conditional Approval is granted, and how fast. Also whether the wireless-only wording of the connectivity prong creates a real escape hatch: the definition lists Wi-Fi, cellular, Bluetooth 'or other similar connections', so a utility-scale unit reaching SCADA over fibre or Ethernet may fall outside — but counsel describe this as a fact-specific, model-by-model question, not a settled carve-out, and it is untested.
regimes.interaction_45x: STACKS WITH, BUT IS NOT THE SAME TEST AS, IRA 45X. 45X is a production tax CREDIT that rewards qualifying US manufacture, with FEOC rules excluding Chinese-origin material; failing it costs you a subsidy. This is a PROHIBITION enforced through equipment authorisation; failing it costs you market access. They diverge on the test itself: 45X domestic-content and FEOC rules are not the Buy American 'domestic end product' test at 48 CFR 25.101(a). A product can qualify for one and fail the other. From 2026-07-28 a manufacturer selling connected inverters into the US must satisfy both regimes independently.
regimes.verification: Verified 2026-08-09 against the FCC Public Notice text (DA-26-786A1) plus client alerts from Stoel Rives, Crowell & Moring, K&L Gates and Morgan Lewis. The operative definitions sit in Appendices B and C of the Notice, which are scanned images without a text layer, so definitional language is taken from counsel summaries corroborated across at least two firms. NOT VERIFIED TO A SECOND SOURCE: a reported step-up of the domestic content threshold to 75% from 2029, and a reported firmware/software waiver expiring 2029-01-01 — both appear in Stoel Rives only and are recorded here as unconfirmed.

programs.title: DoD REE & Critical Mineral Programs
programs.description: Multiple DoD programs supporting domestic REE, antimony, and specialty mineral supply chains. MP Fort Worth magnet plant: DoD floor price $110/kg NdPr, production guaranteed. Lynas Seadrift: DoD-funded HREE separation facility. Perpetua/PPTA: DoD MOU for Stibnite antimony. Materion: defense-critical beryllium supply — Schedule II controlled substance.

programs.title: DOE HALEU Production Program
programs.description: Centrus Energy under DOE contract to produce High-Assay Low-Enriched Uranium (HALEU) for advanced reactors and next-gen naval fuel. Phase III option exercised ($110M through June 2026); 8-year extension options. $2.3B contingent backlog. Centrus is the only US company with active HALEU production capacity.

programs.title: EU Critical Raw Materials Act
programs.description: EU CRM Act (2024): targets 10% domestic extraction, 40% domestic processing, and 25% recycling for strategic minerals by 2030. Also requires sourcing diversification away from single-country suppliers (implicitly targeting China). Strategic Projects designation accelerates permitting. Benefits allied-nation producers with EU ambitions.

levers.title: China REE tranche-2 cliff
levers.description: Second tranche of REE export controls (5 additional elements) scheduled. If implemented, widens the supply shock. If deferred again, may reduce urgency premium — but does not remove the April 2025 controls.
levers.bull_bear: Bull: full implementation widens supply crunch. Bear: further deferral reduces urgency narrative.

levers.title: Section 232 copper tariff decision
levers.description: Commerce Department determination on copper import tariffs. 25% tariff would create a US premium above LME — directly benefiting FCX and SCCO domestic operations.
levers.bull_bear: Bull: tariff creates domestic premium floor. Bear: no action maintains LME parity.

levers.title: Stibnite EIS / Permitting Decision
levers.description: Perpetua Resources Stibnite mine Environmental Impact Statement completion. DoD MOU creates political urgency. Permitting is the only remaining obstacle to the sole significant Western antimony mine.
levers.bull_bear: Bull: EIS approval + DoD funding triggers project FID. Bear: further delay or denial keeps antimony supply structurally short.

levers.title: LME copper inventory / physical squeeze risk
levers.description: LME copper inventories have oscillated sharply. Physical squeeze events (March 2024, potential recurrence) can create extreme backwardation and short-term price spikes. Watch stocks-to-cancel ratios.
levers.bull_bear: Bull: low inventories + demand pull from grid buildout = squeeze risk. Bear: demand softness from China property sector = inventory build.

levers.title: FCC inverter Conditional Approval — who gets cleared, and how fast
levers.description: The live variable in the whole regime. Foreign-produced connected inverters are barred from FCC equipment authorisation unless the Department of War or DHS grants a case-by-case Conditional Approval. Applications go to conditional-approvals@fcc.gov as a machine-readable PDF by 2028-01-01, and must address corporate ownership, product and supply-chain provenance, and a time-bound US manufacturing plan covering capital expenditure, hiring and facility expansion, with ongoing progress reporting. CRITICALLY, NO REVIEW TIMETABLE HAS BEEN PUBLISHED, and as of 2026-08-09 no grant has been reported. Counsel are advising applicants to build agency review time into product launch schedules. The commercial outcome of the rule turns entirely on who clears this queue and when — which means allied manufacturers now hold their US market position at the pleasure of a discretionary licence with no deadline. That asymmetry is what makes this a regime rather than an incident: 'where is it built' has become a first-order question alongside 'who owns the technology'. The 2028-01-01 date on this entry is the APPLICATION deadline, not a decision date.
levers.bull_bear: Bull for names that can certify >65% domestic content, and for the US component tier that has to supply it — power semiconductors, magnetics, copper windings, passives. Bear for anyone dependent on a new foreign-built connected SKU, and for project timelines if the approval queue stalls. Watch for the first grant as the signal that the process functions at all.
